blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The income statement is also called the profit and loss statement. It shows how much a company earned and how much it spent. The period is usually a month, a quarter or a year. The difference between them is the profit or the loss.

At Czarnikow, the income statement shows revenue from sugar trading, freight services and advisory work. Below revenue, you see the cost of goods sold. Then you see operating expenses, like salaries, rent and technology. The bottom line tells you if the company made money or not.

Reading an income statement is a basic skill in business. You do not need to be an accountant. You just need to understand where the money comes from and where it goes.

items.q: What is another name for the income statement?
items.why: "The income statement is also called the profit and loss statement."

items.q: What period does an income statement usually cover?
options: A month, a quarter or a year
items.why: "The period is usually a month, a quarter or a year."

items.q: Which of these is an operating expense in the text?
items.why: "operating expenses, like salaries, rent and technology."

items.q: The text suggests that reading a P&L is…
items.why: Inferência: "You do not need to be an accountant" — qualquer pessoa de negócios pode ler.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: the bottom line is the least important number
the bottom line answers if the company made money
revenue is not shown on the statement
items.why: Inferência: "The bottom line tells you if the company made money or not."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando o P&L a um novo analista. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, come and look at this page with me. This is our monthly P&L. It is only one page, but it tells the whole story.

We start at the top. This first line is revenue. This is all the money we earn from sugar trading, from freight, and from advisory work. So the top line is what comes in.

Now we go down. The next line is the cost of goods sold. Then we have our expenses. See here — salaries, rent, and technology. We take revenue, and we subtract each cost, line by line.

And here, at the bottom, is the answer. This is the bottom line. Revenue minus all the expenses. If the number is positive, we made a profit this period. If it is negative, we made a loss.

This month the bottom line is green, so we are fine. Every department reviews this page every month. It is simple, but it is the most important page you will read.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Where does Sophie say the revenue line is?
items.why: "We start at the top. This first line is revenue."

items.q: What does Sophie do with revenue and the costs?
options: She subtracts each cost, line by line
items.why: "We take revenue, and we subtract each cost, line by line."

items.q: This month, the bottom line is green. What does that mean?
items.why: Inferência: verde = número positivo = lucro. "If the number is positive, we made a profit."

items.q: Why does Sophie say the page is important?
options: Because every department reviews it every month
Because only she can read it
Because it shows the office rent
items.why: "Every department reviews this page every month… the most important page you will read."

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ela explica com calma, passo a passo, para ensinar o novo analista.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our revenue grew this year." Revenue is…
items.why: Revenue = receita: o dinheiro que a empresa ganha.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We spent too much this month, so we made a ___."
items.why: Loss = prejuízo: quando as despesas passam da receita.

items.q: "Salaries and rent are a big expense for us." An expense is…
items.why: Expense = despesa: dinheiro que sai da empresa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The report covers one ___: the month of June."
items.why: Period = período: o intervalo de tempo do relatório.

items.q: "After all the costs, we still made a profit." A profit is…
items.why: Profit = lucro: o que sobra depois de tirar as despesas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre resultados. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's look at the bottom line." The bottom line is…
options: the final profit or loss figure
items.why: Bottom line = a linha final do P&L: o lucro ou prejuízo.

items.q: "Our costs are going up, so profit is going down." To go up means to…
items.why: Go up = subir, aumentar.

items.q: "The boss has to sign off on the report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We need to cut costs next quarter." To cut costs means to…
items.why: Cut costs = cortar custos, gastar menos.

items.q: "Sales this month added up to two million dollars." To add up to means to…
items.why: Add up to = somar, chegar a um total.
